title: Halftone print screens: CMYK, comic dots, newsprint, duotone
purpose: Generate tileable maps of printed halftone: a procedural design separated into inks and screened as round dots on rotated whole-number lattices at classic angles, with misregistration, dot gain and fibrous aged paper. Use for comic and pop-art surfaces, posters, newspapers, packaging and print-themed backgrounds.

contract.signature: generate(width=256, height=256, seed=0, preset="default", directx_normal=False, **parameters) -> {map name: {"channels", "colour_space", "pixels"}}
contract.command_line: python halftone_print.py --size 1024 --seed 7 --preset NAME --out DIR [--width W --height H] [--set NAME=VALUE] [--directx-normal] [--orm]

parameters.meaning: Features of the printed design across the tile.

parameters.name: misregister
parameters.meaning: Offset between the ink screens, as on a loose press.

parameters.name: dot_gain
parameters.meaning: Dots printing larger than their coverage, as ink spreads in the paper.

parameters.name: yellowing

limits: Amplitude-modulated round dots only: no stochastic, line or elliptical screens. Screen angles are rounded to whole-number lattice vectors so the screen repeats, which moves them by up to a few degrees from the nominal angle at low line counts. The separation is a simple grey-component replacement without colour management or ink limits, inks multiply as ideal transparent filters, and dot gain is a curve rather than ink spreading. The printed design is procedural noise, not artwork. Fine screens alias below about four pixels per dot row.
technique_references: Amplitude-modulated halftoning with a round-dot spot function
Screen lattices from whole-number vectors for exact tiling
Classic screen angles: cyan 15, magenta 75, yellow 0, black 45 degrees
